explanation.summary: Bisector equation of $x^2 - 2mxy - y^2 = 0$ is $\frac{x^2 - y^2}{1 - (-1)} = \frac{xy}{-m} \implies m(x^2 - y^2) + 2xy = 0 \implies x^2 + \frac{2}{m}xy - y^2 = 0$. Comparing with $x^2 - 2nxy - y^2 = 0 \implies -2n = 2/m \implies mn + 1 = 0$.

questions.questionText: Derivative of $\sin^2 x$ with respect to $2x^2$ is:

explanation.summary: $\frac{d(\sin^2 x)/dx}{d(2x^2)/dx} = \frac{2\sin x\cos x}{4x} = \frac{\sin 2x}{4x}$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: $\frac{d(\sin^2 x)/dx}{d(2x^2)/dx} = \frac{2\sin x\cos x}{4x} = \frac{\sin 2x}{4x}$.

questions.questionText: If $f(x) = \det\begin{bmatrix} x & 8 & 8 \\ 2 & x & 8 \\ 2 & 2 & x \end{bmatrix}$, then $f(x)$ has a local maximum at:

explanation.summary: Evaluating determinant and finding critical points yields local maximum at $x = -4$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: Evaluating determinant and finding critical points yields local maximum at $x = -4$.

questions.questionText: Consider $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$. Then $A^3 - 9A$ is:

explanation.summary: Using Cayley-Hamilton theorem, $A^3 - 9A$ simplifies to a diagonal matrix.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: Using Cayley-Hamilton theorem, $A^3 - 9A$ simplifies to a diagonal matrix.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: $\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{1}{k(k+1)}$ is equal to:

explanation.summary: Telescoping series: $\sum_{k=1}^n (\frac{1}{k} - \frac{1}{k+1}) = 1 - \frac{1}{n+1} = \frac{n}{n+1}$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: Telescoping series: $\sum_{k=1}^n (\frac{1}{k} - \frac{1}{k+1}) = 1 - \frac{1}{n+1} = \frac{n}{n+1}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: Find a value of $\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2 + 2\cos 4\theta}}$:

explanation.summary: $\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2(1+\cos 4\theta)}} = \sqrt{2 + 2\cos 2\theta} = \sqrt{2(1+\cos 2\theta)} = 2\cos\theta$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: $\sqrt{2 + \sqrt{2(1+\cos 4\theta)}} = \sqrt{2 + 2\cos 2\theta} = \sqrt{2(1+\cos 2\theta)} = 2\cos\theta$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.questionText: The value of $\sin(2\sin^{-1}(0.6))$ is:

explanation.summary: Let $\theta = \sin^{-1}(0.6) \implies \sin\theta = 0.6 = 3/5, \cos\theta = 0.8 = 4/5$. $\sin(2\theta) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 2(0.6)(0.8) = 0.96$.

stepByStep.title: Official Solution
stepByStep.content: Let $\theta = \sin^{-1}(0.6) \implies \sin\theta = 0.6 = 3/5, \cos\theta = 0.8 = 4/5$. $\sin(2\theta) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 2(0.6)(0.8) = 0.96$.
